sample_unit: census tracts (plus 20 high-diabetes tracts in a chatbot pilot)

links.outcome: Accuracy of store and place names chatbots recommended for local food access
links.effect: Of 55 places named, 13% had errors, and most were over a mile away.
links.quote: Of 55 places they named, 13% had errors, and most were over a mile away.

links.outcome: Whether chatbot meal advice was healthy and fit local food access in high-diabetes tracts
links.effect: Advice was healthy, but in hidden food-desert tracts 30% of recommended foods were not reliably sold nearby; chatbots barely adjusted.
links.quote: Chatbot advice was healthy, but in hidden tracts 30% of recommended foods were not reliably sold nearby; the chatbots barely adjusted.

unlisted_practices: Place-aware check of AI diet advice built on public food-access data
Using large-grocery-store-only food access maps rather than all SNAP-authorized stores to identify food deserts

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of commercial LLM chatbots generating diabetic meal plans across census tracts to assess feasibility and food-access alignment; does not test a specific deployment safeguard/practice implementation comparative intervention.
